name: capture
description: A client, a router that can add delay and loss (pathlab), and a server with DNS, HTTP and HTTPS: what tcpdump can miss (--immediate-mode, kernel drops, snaplen), capturing on -i any, localizing a drop with captures at four points, ring buffers, network vs server time and one-way delay from two captures, TCP loss as the sender's and the receiver's capture report it, zero window in Expert Info, unanswered DNS queries, and TLS without and with a key log.

nodes.name: router
setup: ip tuntap add dev pl-ab mode tun && ip tuntap add dev pl-ba mode tun && ip link set pl-ab up && ip link set pl-ba up && sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.pl-ab.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.pl-ba.rp_filter=0 && ip rule add iif eth0 table 100 && ip route add default dev pl-ab table 100 && ip rule add iif eth1 table 101 && ip route add default dev pl-ba table 101

checks.name: stop tcpdump right after the traffic WITHOUT --immediate-mode: the packets were 'received by filter' but never written — libpcap hands them over in blocks
run: for m in '' '--immediate-mode'; do tcpdump $m -Z root -U -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/immediate.pcap icmp 2>${EVIDENCE}/immediate.log & T=$!; sleep 0.7; ping -c3 -i 0.002 -q 198.18.211.10 >/dev/null; kill -INT $T; wait $T; echo "tcpdump ${m:-(default)}: $(grep -E 'captured|received' ${EVIDENCE}/immediate.log | tr '\n' ' ')"; done
expect_contains: (default): 0 packets captured 6 packets received by filter
--immediate-mode: 6 packets captured 6 packets received by filter

checks.name: -i any on the router: one ping appears twice per direction — in on eth0, out on eth1 — with the Linux 'cooked' link type instead of Ethernet
run: tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i any -w ${EVIDENCE}/any.pcap icmp 2>${EVIDENCE}/any.log & T=$!; sleep 0.7; ip netns exec nl-capture-client ping -c1 -q 198.18.211.10 >/dev/null; sleep 0.3; kill -INT $T; wait $T; grep -o 'link-type [A-Z0-9_]*' ${EVIDENCE}/any.log; tcpdump -nn -r ${EVIDENCE}/any.pcap 2>/dev/null
expect_contains: eth0  In  IP 198.18.210.10 > 198.18.211.10: ICMP echo request
eth1  Out IP 198.18.210.10 > 198.18.211.10: ICMP echo request

checks.name: find where packets die: capture at four points while the router drops one port — the SYNs are seen leaving the client and entering the router, never leaving it
run: ip netns exec nl-capture-router iptables -I FORWARD -p tcp --dport 7021 -j DROP; P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/drop-client.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drop-client.log & P="$P $!"; ip netns exec nl-capture-router tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/drop-router-in.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drop-router-in.log & P="$P $!"; ip netns exec nl-capture-router tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth1 -w ${EVIDENCE}/drop-router-out.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drop-router-out.log & P="$P $!"; ip netns exec nl-capture-server tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/drop-server.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drop-server.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; ${BIN}/tcplab dial -to 198.18.211.10:7021 -timeout 2.5s; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-capture-router iptables -D FORWARD -p tcp --dport 7021 -j DROP; for p in client router-in router-out server; do echo "SYNs seen at $p: $(tcpdump -nn -r ${EVIDENCE}/drop-$p.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] == tcp-syn' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"; done

checks.name: snaplen 96 keeps the headers and the first 30 bytes of payload (enough for 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK', not for the body): a fraction of the file size, every data frame marked as cut short
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -s 96 -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/snap96.pcap 'tcp port 8080' 2>${EVIDENCE}/snap96.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  curl -s -o /dev/null http://198.18.211.10:8080/obj?size=20000; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/snapfull.pcap 'tcp port 8080' 2>${EVIDENCE}/snapfull.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  curl -s -o /dev/null http://198.18.211.10:8080/obj?size=20000; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; for f in snap96 snapfull; do echo "$f: $(capinfos -c -s ${EVIDENCE}/$f.pcap | grep -E 'Number of packets|File size' | tr -s ' ' | tr '\n' ' ') HTTP status lines: $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/$f.pcap -Y http.response.code -T fields -e http.response.code 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '), frames cut short: $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/$f.pcap -Y '_ws.short' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"; done

checks.name: a capture can miss packets: a small capture buffer (-B 64 KiB) feeding a reader that stalls for 3 s drops almost everything — tcpdump reports it when it stops; a large buffer writing to a file kept up
run: rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/slow.fifo; mkfifo ${EVIDENCE}/slow.fifo; (exec 3<${EVIDENCE}/slow.fifo; sleep 3; cat <&3 >/dev/null) & R=$!; tcpdump -B 64 -nn -v -i eth0 'tcp port 5201' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drops-slow.log >${EVIDENCE}/slow.fifo & T=$!; sleep 0.7; iperf3 -c 198.18.211.10 -t 1 >/dev/null; sleep 2.5; kill -INT $T; wait $T $R; tcpdump -B 16384 -s 96 -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/drops-fast.pcap 'tcp port 5201' 2>${EVIDENCE}/drops-fast.log & T=$!; sleep 0.7; iperf3 -c 198.18.211.10 -t 1 >/dev/null; sleep 0.3; kill -INT $T; wait $T; for f in slow fast; do echo "$f: $(grep -E 'captured|received|dropped' ${EVIDENCE}/drops-$f.log | tr '\n' ' ')"; done
expect_contains: received by filter 0 packets dropped by kernel

checks.name: a ring buffer (-C 1 -W 3): at most three files of 1 MB each, the oldest overwritten — bounded disk however long it runs
run: mkdir -p ${EVIDENCE}/ring && tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -C 1 -W 3 -w ${EVIDENCE}/ring/ring.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>/dev/null & T=$!; sleep 0.7; ${BIN}/tcplab send -to 198.18.211.10:7021 -bytes 20000000 >/dev/null; sleep 0.3; kill -INT $T; wait $T; ls -l ${EVIDENCE}/ring | awk 'NR>1 {print $5, $9}'; echo "files: $(ls ${EVIDENCE}/ring | wc -l)"; capinfos -a -e ${EVIDENCE}/ring/ring.pcap0 | grep -E 'First|Last'

checks.name: one request captured at both ends: the handshake gives the RTT (≈ 21 ms on both sides), the first response byte separates server time (≈ 200 ms at the server) from network time
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/time-client.pcap 'tcp port 8080' 2>${EVIDENCE}/time-client.log & P="$P $!"; ip netns exec nl-capture-server tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/time-server.pcap 'tcp port 8080' 2>${EVIDENCE}/time-server.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'curl: connect %{time_connect} s, first byte %{time_starttransfer} s, total %{time_total} s\n' 'http://198.18.211.10:8080/obj?size=2000&delay=200ms'; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; for p in client server; do echo "$p capture: initial RTT $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/time-$p.pcap -Y 'tcp.analysis.initial_rtt' -T fields -e tcp.analysis.initial_rtt 2>/dev/null | head -1) s, request→first response packet $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/time-$p.pcap -o tcp.desegment_tcp_streams:FALSE -Y http.response -T fields -e http.time 2>/dev/null) s"; done; tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/time-client.pcap -q -z follow,tcp,ascii,0 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(GET|HTTP|Host)'

checks.name: merge the two captures (same clock here): the SYN left the client and reached the server ≈ 10 ms later — a one-way delay; across hosts this needs synchronized clocks
run: mergecap -w ${EVIDENCE}/time-merged.pcap ${EVIDENCE}/time-client.pcap ${EVIDENCE}/time-server.pcap && tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/time-merged.pcap -Y 'tcp.flags.syn==1 && tcp.flags.ack==0' -T fields -e frame.time_epoch -e ip.id -e tcp.seq_raw 2>/dev/null | awk '{t[NR]=$1; id[NR]=$2} END {printf "SYN ip.id %s: seen %d times, one-way delay %.1f ms\n", id[1], NR, (t[2]-t[1])*1000}'

checks.name: one lossy 5 MB transfer captured at both ends: the sender's capture shows retransmissions; the receiver's shows 'previous segment not captured', out-of-order and duplicate ACKs — the same loss, two vocabularies
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -s 128 -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/loss-client.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/loss-client.log & P="$P $!"; ip netns exec nl-capture-server tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -s 128 -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/loss-server.pcap 'tcp port 7021' 2>${EVIDENCE}/loss-server.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; ${BIN}/tcplab send -to 198.18.211.10:7021 -bytes 5000000 -timeout 30s | grep -E 'transfer|retransmitted'; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; ip netns exec nl-capture-router ${BIN}/pathlab set loss=0 rate=0 >/dev/null; printf '%-38s %8s %8s\n' 'display filter' sender receiver; for flt in tcp.analysis.retransmission tcp.analysis.fast_retransmission tcp.analysis.lost_segment tcp.analysis.out_of_order tcp.analysis.duplicate_ack tcp.options.sack_le; do printf '%-38s %8s %8s\n' $flt $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/loss-client.pcap -Y $flt 2>/dev/null | wc -l) $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/loss-server.pcap -Y $flt 2>/dev/null | wc -l); done; tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/loss-client.pcap -q -z conv,tcp 2>/dev/null | grep -A3 'Frames'

checks.name: a receiver that never reads: Expert Info flags the zero window and the window-full sends — and labels Linux's persist probes 'keep-alive'
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/zerowin.pcap 'tcp port 7020' 2>${EVIDENCE}/zerowin.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; ${BIN}/tcplab send -to 198.18.211.10:7020 -bytes 1000000 -timeout 4s | grep -E 'transfer|persist|probes'; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; for flt in tcp.analysis.zero_window tcp.analysis.zero_window_probe tcp.analysis.window_full; do echo "$flt: $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/zerowin.pcap -Y $flt 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"; done; tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/zerowin.pcap -q -z expert 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ +Sequence'

checks.name: three DNS outcomes in one capture: an answer, NXDOMAIN, and a query whose response the router drops — 'dns.flags.response == 0 && !dns.response_in' (two-pass: -2) finds the unanswered one
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/dns.pcap 'udp port 53' 2>${EVIDENCE}/dns.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; dig +short +tries=1 +time=1 api.capture.test; dig +tries=1 +time=1 nope.capture.test | grep -o 'status: [A-Z]*'; ip netns exec nl-capture-router iptables -I FORWARD -p udp --sport 53 -j DROP; dig +tries=1 +time=1 lost.capture.test | grep -E 'timed out|no servers'; ip netns exec nl-capture-router iptables -D FORWARD -p udp --sport 53 -j DROP; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; echo answered:; tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/dns.pcap -Y 'dns.flags.response==1' -T fields -e dns.qry.name -e dns.flags.rcode -e dns.time -e dns.a 2>/dev/null; echo unanswered:; tshark -2 -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/dns.pcap -Y 'dns.flags.response==0 && !dns.response_in' -T fields -e dns.qry.name 2>/dev/null

checks.name: three HTTPS requests with curl (OpenSSL): untrusted CA, trusted (TLS 1.3), trusted with TLS 1.2 — SSLKEYLOGFILE records the session secrets
run: P=''; ip netns exec nl-capture-client tcpdump -Z root --immediate-mode -nn -i eth0 -w ${EVIDENCE}/tls.pcap 'tcp port 8443' 2>${EVIDENCE}/tls.log & P="$P $!"; sleep 0.7; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  SSLKEYLOGFILE=${EVIDENCE}/tls-keys.log curl -sS --http1.1 https://api.capture.test:8443/ 2>&1 | head -1; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  SSLKEYLOGFILE=${EVIDENCE}/tls-keys.log curl -sS --http1.1 --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/webpki/ca.pem https://api.capture.test:8443/obj?size=10; echo; unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy;  SSLKEYLOGFILE=${EVIDENCE}/tls-keys.log curl -sS --http1.1 --tls-max 1.2 --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/webpki/ca.pem https://api.capture.test:8443/ -o /dev/null; sleep 0.4; kill -INT $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; echo "key log: $(wc -l < ${EVIDENCE}/tls-keys.log) lines, labels: $(cut -d' ' -f1 ${EVIDENCE}/tls-keys.log | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"

checks.name: WITHOUT keys: SNI and ALPN are in clear text; TLS 1.3 hides the certificate, TLS 1.2 shows it; OpenSSL's 'Unknown CA' alert went out unencrypted; no HTTP is visible
run: tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/tls.pcap -Y 'tls.handshake.type==1 || tls.handshake.type==11 || tls.alert_message' -T fields -e tcp.stream -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name -e tls.handshake.extensions_alpn_str -e x509ce.dNSName -e tls.alert_message.desc -e _ws.col.Info 2>/dev/null; echo "HTTP messages visible: $(tshark -n -r ${EVIDENCE}/tls.pcap -Y http 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"

checks.name: WITH the key log: the requests, responses and close_notify alerts are readable
